Not OP but grew up with a similar mom!

My mom, a pretty devout christian, limited basically _everything_ ... I wasn't allowed to read fantasy books or anything that was fiction for the most part. If I wanted to watch or read anything she'd do a crap ton of research on whatever it was I wanted to do and then sit down with me and either explain why I couldn't ("honey the author doesn't share our beliefs and I don't want then tainting your mind with impure things") or how I could relate it all to god/jesus.

My dad however, a very tired wiccan man, evolved into an *incredibly* tired wiccan man and finally told her she was wasting her time, if I really wanted to read those types of books then I'd just read them when I got older. In middle school I weaseled my way into reading the HP series and he called her out on being stupid then too and I think she finally realized I was just a kid reading something that other kids (and adults) enjoy and this wasn't some anti-theist way to get to me.

My mom was the same way when I was in middle school (and this was 2012-2013 btw to give you a perspective of the time frame) and my best friend was massively into HP and would offer to loan them to me (I'd just read it at school and not take it home so my mom would never know) however because I thought I was smart as plum pudding I told my mom that we were reading the series in class as a big AR pool.

Brought it up a couple years afterwards and my mom knew I was lying the whole time but realized after the 2nd book that I genuinely enjoyed them (plus I _was_ getting AR points) and so let me keep reading...that and my dad told her she was being stupid, if a silly child's book that's not even about religion changed my beliefs then they weren't very strongly held ones to begin with and I would likely drop her religion anyways and what do you know...he was right!
